intro: Solomon Islands is a scattered nation of nearly 1,000 islands in the south-west Pacific, scene of fierce World War Two battles.

chapters.title: Early settlers
text: People have lived here for about 30,000 years. Spanish explorer Álvaro de Mendaña arrived in 1568 and named the islands after King Solomon, hoping for gold.

chapters.title: Protectorate and war
text: Britain made the islands a protectorate in the 1890s. In 1942–43 the Battle of Guadalcanal between Japan and the US was a turning point in the Pacific war. Solomon Islander scouts helped rescue John F. Kennedy after his boat sank.

highlight.title: Guadalcanal
highlight.text: One of the most important battles of the Pacific war.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Solomon Islands became independent in 1978. Ethnic tensions from 1998 to 2003, 'the Tensions', led to an Australian-led peacekeeping mission, RAMSI. In 2019 the country switched recognition from Taiwan to China.

keyTerms.meaning: A territory protected and run by another country.
